title: audit_anatomy audits zero files by default and reports clean

evidence.after: runAudit({ path: <repo>, mode: 'full' }) -> totalFiles=4121, findings=3083 (error 2, warn 3081)
evidence.control: runAudit({ ..., files: [192 literal .tsx paths] }) -> totalFiles=192, findings=88 (unchanged by this fix)
evidence.revert_test: 3 of 5 regression assertions fail with the fix reverted, 5 of 5 pass with it restored

assumptions: Fork D resolved to D1 by the human before dispatch: reuse the shared scan-target resolution the sibling check-design verifiers use, so all verifiers in one run agree on their file set. SECURITY_SCAN_GLOB was explicitly ruled out as the wrong boundary for component anatomy.

The correct sibling is detect-drift's collectFiles (packages/cli/src/drift/index.ts): explicit `files` wins and bypasses excludes, otherwise walk the project root honouring design.exclude union analysis.exclude.

Took the extraction rather than a local fix, per the packages/core/src/security/scan-targets.ts precedent — that file exists because three copy-pasted glob literals had already drifted. The extraction wires audit-anatomy, detect-drift and audit-brand to one collectDesignScanFiles.

audit-brand-compliance now honours design.exclude / analysis.exclude, which it previously ignored. This only ever narrows its file set and is the behaviour design.exclude is documented to have; it is the price of 'all verifiers agree on their file set'. naming-craft keeps its own code-only extension list and was deliberately left alone: it is not one of the four check-design verifiers.
An empty `files: []` is now the absence of scoping (walk the project), not a request to audit nothing — the semantic detect-drift and audit-brand already used.

A resolved scope of zero files throws. check-design records the throw under verifiersFailed and exits 2 (degraded) rather than printing a clean audit; this matches the repo's no-silent-abstention doctrine (output/formatter.ts, mcp/tools/validate.ts, commands/roadmap/sync-verdict.ts).

tests/design-pipeline/integration/end-to-end.test.ts ran its 'default run' assertion against a completely empty temp directory and now gets the abstention. The fixture was given one source file; the test's intent (all four verifiers register and run) is unchanged.

NOT FIXED, reported as follow-ups: (1) the ANAT-P* pattern catalog fires heavily on non-UI .ts files (test files, server handlers) now that the default scope includes them — the great majority of the 3,081 new warn findings are false positives and the catalog needs a component-file gate; (2) design-pipeline still returns verdict 'pass' when a verifier lands in verifiersFailed; (3) the two error-severity ANAT-D findings this fix surfaced on this repository (a core test fixture Button.jsx and packages/dashboard EmptyState.tsx) are real and left unfixed, as fixing them is outside a CLI bug lane.
